assumptions: A meaningful number of Polish advisers handle repeated AI governance dossiers rather than isolated engagements.
Advisers will pay for delivery efficiency while retaining ownership of their methods and end-client relationships.
Public law plus properly licensed references are sufficient to maintain a useful product without copying protected standards.
Scheduled expert review can keep mappings reliable without turning the company into bespoke legal consulting.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Prepaid licenses from multiple unrelated advisers, repeated dossier usage, measured setup-time and review-finding reductions, renewal or expansion intent, licensed-content costs, expert maintenance hours, and proof of a lawful data-learning loop.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Licensing a continuously maintained local evidence system to advisers converts repeated compliance delivery into reusable product economics instead of open-ended founder consulting.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Consultancies repeatedly assemble dossiers and bear stale-template rework, but no adviser has shown that the problem is costly enough to overcome preference for proprietary methods or free official material.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepaid annual licenses and per-dossier fees offer attractive capital-light repeat revenue, although target pricing, adviser volume, legal-update cost, support burden, and acquisition payback are unvalidated.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish compliance and quality advisers form a focused, reachable beachhead, but the number with repeated in-scope dossiers and sufficient software budget is unknown.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Polish language, adviser neutrality, and white labeling help, but consultancies, law firms, standards publishers, and global governance suites can author or localize similar structures.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful evidence engine could extend to more adviser types, additional EU languages, adjacent standards, and other recurring regulated dossiers.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Owned code and versioned mappings are durable assets, and consented completeness failures may improve them, but copyright protects expression rather than the underlying compliance method.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The founder can independently create the product and fits evidence automation, but has no demonstrated adviser channel, regulatory reputation, exclusive content right, or customer-derived corpus.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Active AI Act implementation and evolving standards create immediate demand for version provenance and repeatable evidence collection, while also increasing maintenance pressure.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Direct adviser outreach, auditor relationships, and professional education are feasible focused routes, but no partner, audience, or license relationship is presently controlled.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A narrow software and template product is feasible within the stated capital and schedule, though legal accuracy, standards licensing, product-versus-assurance boundaries, and continuous updates remain material risks.

highest_value_structural_change: Turn the template license into an adviser-of-record workflow distributed through a signed professional or audit channel, with permissioned cross-dossier completeness benchmarks that improve outcomes without exposing client data.
main_structural_strength: The founder can own the core software and authored schema outright, producing a capital-light reusable license tied to advisers' existing billable dossier events.
primary_score_limiter: The apparent moat is mostly replicable compliance structure, and adviser willingness to replace proprietary methods with a recurring external royalty is wholly unproven.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Consultancies may prefer their own templates and official sources, while larger governance platforms and law firms can localize equivalent evidence workflows as part of broader offerings.
